hist-20c-01-c3.text: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum. Documenting Numbers of Victims of the Holocaust and Nazi Persecution. Holocaust Encyclopedia, United States Holocaust Memorial Museum.
hist-20c-01-c3.quote: The Nazis and their allies and collaborators killed six million Jewish people.

hist-20c-02-c2.text: history.state.gov. Milestones in the History of U.S. Foreign Relations - Office of the Historian. history.state.gov.
hist-20c-02-c2.quote: The Cuban Missile Crisis of October 1962 was a direct and dangerous confrontation between the United States and the Soviet Union during the Cold War and was the moment when the two superpowers came closest to nuclear conflict.
hist-20c-02-c2.claim: The Cuban Missile Crisis (October 1962), when Soviet nuclear missiles were discovered in Cuba, brought the world the closest it has ever come to nuclear war.

hist-20c-04-c1.quote: The world's first nuclear explosion occurred on July 16, 1945, when a plutonium implosion device was tested at a site located 210 miles south of Los Alamos, New Mexico
hist-20c-04-c1.claim: The first nuclear test (Trinity) occurred on July 16, 1945, in New Mexico.
